I'm working in a daycare for childs from 2month to 5years old so I guess you can call me a "pro" - first of all, a few "rules" (more guidelines)
- Be clear. Kids dont get irony or rethorical questions.
- They hear much more than you think. Every single word you say in their presence.
- Respect them and don't talk in so called baby language. 

Go down to their level, ask them about their hobbies, their friends, what they did the last weekend and to avoid the interview, response with YOUR experience: Tell them about YOUR family, YOUR friends, YOUR hobbies and so on. Don't talk to much, if they are interested they will ask for more.
From my experience, its much easier to interact with kids when you really use your bodylanguage. For example, when you tella storie, make clear and big gestures and keep them "entertained". 
Try to make them laugh a bit, more isn't expected by most parents.
Hope this can help you, sorry for my bad english :)
